input_signals.name: Working-Capital Secured Cheapness
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), INDICATOR(SUB(RATIO(wcap, at), RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)), 0))
input_signals.hypothesis: Book-to-market works better when the cheap firm has a working-capital cushion that exceeds its debt burden.
input_signals.reasoning: Deep value stocks with weak liquidity can remain cheap because equity holders face financing risk and creditor pressure. This conditional signal activates book-to-market only when net working capital relative to assets is stronger than total debt relative to assets, identifying cheap firms with near-term solvency support.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), indicator( sub( ratio( wcap, at ), ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ) ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Taxpaying Deep Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MUL(INDICATOR(pi, 0), INDICATOR(txt, 0)))
input_signals.hypothesis: High book-to-market firms that still generate positive pretax income and incur taxes are more likely to be viable value opportunities than distressed cheap firms consuming loss carryforwards.
input_signals.reasoning: The distress filter is based on current taxable going-concern status rather than accumulated retained earnings, avoiding a retained-earnings-to-market decomposition. Cheap firms with positive pretax income and tax expense are less likely to be equity-stub lottery stocks whose low valuation reflects severe operating distress.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), mul( indicator( pi, 0 ), indicator( txt, 0 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liquidity-Backed EBITDA Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(che, dlc), lct)))
input_signals.hypothesis: EBITDA cheapness should be more strongly rewarded when the firm has enough cash after near-term debt to withstand current-liability pressure.
input_signals.reasoning: The valuation leg uses operating earnings yield, while the distress leg separately measures short-run liquidity capacity, so the signal does not double-count operating cash flow. Cheap firms with a liquidity runway are less likely to be forced into dilutive financing, fire sales, or default before value can mean-revert.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( che, dlc ), lct ) ) )

input_signals.name: Creditor-Claim Earnings Yield
input_signals.expression: RATIO(ib, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), MAX(ADD(dltt, dlc), SUB(lt, che))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Earnings yield should predict returns more reliably when earnings are high relative to both equity value and creditor-claim overhang.
input_signals.reasoning: A high equity earnings yield can be misleading for highly levered firms because equity is a thin residual claim. Scaling income by market equity plus the larger of funded debt and net-liability overhang embeds distress directly into the valuation denominator, avoiding an accrual-quality repackaging and keeping the expected sign coherent.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( ib, add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), max( add( dltt, dlc ), sub( lt, che ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Burn Maturity-Wall Trap
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dlc, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MUL(INDICATOR(NEG(oancf), 0), RANK(RATIO(NEG(oancf), act))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with short-term debt large relative to market equity should underperform when they are also burning operating cash.
input_signals.reasoning: The expression no longer double-counts current liabilities and does not treat leverage-to-market as automatically bad. The negative signal is confined to firms where a maturity wall coincides with operating cash burn, making the low equity value more likely to reflect imminent financing distress than a compensated leverage premium.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( dlc, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), mul( indicator( neg( oancf ), 0 ), rank( ratio( neg( oancf ), act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Operating-Liquidity Sales Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(revt, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), revt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Revenue-cheap firms are more attractive when their sales base is supported by positive operating liquidity rather than current-liability pressure.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids using low profitability as the distress leg, so it is not simply a profitability anomaly disguised as a sales-yield trap. The interaction asks whether low price-to-sales reflects an undervalued operating franchise with working-capital support, rather than a distressed firm generating sales that cannot translate into equity value.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( revt, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), revt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Net-Liability EBITDA Improvement Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(lt, che), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: EBITDA-cheap firms should earn higher returns when net liability burden is falling rather than rising.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests a distress trajectory channel rather than another static liquidity screen. Cheap operating earnings are more credible for equity holders when liabilities net of cash are declining relative to assets, because improving claim structure reduces the chance that future operating gains accrue primarily to creditors.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( neg( delta( ratio( sub( lt, che ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Tax-Remittance EBITDA Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(txt, lct)))
input_signals.hypothesis: EBITDA-cheap firms should perform better when they are generating taxable income large enough to matter relative to near-term obligations.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids an enterprise-value denominator and instead tests whether the EBITDA yield is validated by actual tax remittance capacity under current-liability pressure. Cheap EBITDA without taxes may reflect accounting operating income that is not translating into a solvent going-concern claim for equity holders.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( txt, lct ) ) )

input_signals.name: Supplier-Pressure Relief Sales Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(revt, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(lct, revt), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Revenue-cheap firms should earn higher returns when current-liability pressure per dollar of revenue is falling.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces book-to-market times profitability improvement with a liability-pressure trajectory, avoiding a direct Piotroski-style value recovery screen. The mechanism is that cheap sales are more likely to be recoverable franchise value when payables, accruals, and other current claims are not expanding relative to the sales base.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( revt, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( neg( delta( ratio( lct, revt ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Buffered OCF Yield
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(che, dlc), lct)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating-cash-flow yield should be most rewarded when the firm also has cash remaining after short-term debt relative to current liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: This repairs the earlier OCF double-counting failure by using operating cash flow only in the valuation leg and an independent balance-sheet liquidity cushion in the distress leg. Cheap cash-flow firms with enough cash to absorb near-term claims are less likely to require distressed financing before value realization.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( che, dlc ), lct ) ) )

input_signals.name: Long-Runway EBITDA Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: EBITDA-cheap firms should perform better when liabilities are not concentrated in debt due within one year.
input_signals.reasoning: High EBITDA-to-price can be a value opportunity or a thin equity stub facing imminent rollover risk. Conditioning on a lower short-term-debt share of total liabilities focuses on firms with more time for operating value to accrue to equity holders rather than creditors.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( neg( ratio( dlc, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Claim-Cushioned Sales Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(revt, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Revenue-cheap firms should outperform when net current assets provide a cushion against total liability claims.
input_signals.reasoning: Prior sales-value liquidity measures risked rewarding working-capital bloat when scaling net current assets by sales. Scaling the net current asset surplus by total liabilities instead asks whether the sales franchise is cheap while the balance sheet still protects the residual equity claim.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( revt, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: EBITDA Cash-Cushion Momentum Spread
input_signals.expression: SUB(MIN(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(che, dlc), lct), 1))), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(che, dlc), lct), 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: EBITDA-cheap firms should earn higher returns when their cash cushion against short-term claims is improving rather than deteriorating.
input_signals.reasoning: This builds on the successful liquidity-backed operating-value channel but tests a distress-resolution mechanism rather than another static liquidity level. The spread emphasizes cheap EBITDA firms with improving cash-surplus coverage and de-emphasizes cheap firms whose liquidity cushion is being depleted.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( min( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( delta( ratio( sub( che, dlc ), lct ), 1 ) ) ), min( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( neg( delta( ratio( sub( che, dlc ), lct ), 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Deficit-Adjusted EBITDA Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, MAX(NEG(re), 0)), lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: EBITDA-cheap firms should outperform when their equity cushion has not been hollowed out by accumulated retained deficits relative to liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from another EBITDA-yield times near-term-liquidity variant and instead tests whether the residual equity claim is economically intact after cumulative losses. Cheap EBITDA is more likely to accrue to shareholders when liabilities are backed by equity capital that has not already been consumed by a retained deficit.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( ceq, max( neg( re ), 0 ) ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Sales Franchise Solvency Spread
input_signals.expression: SUB(MUL(RANK(RATIO(revt, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MUL(INDICATOR(SUB(act, lct), 0), INDICATOR(re, 0))), MUL(RANK(RATIO(revt, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MUL(INDICATOR(SUB(lct, act), 0), INDICATOR(NEG(re), 0))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Revenue-cheap firms with positive current-asset coverage and positive retained earnings should outperform revenue-cheap firms with negative working capital and retained deficits.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the incoherent negative multiplicative trap structure by explicitly contrasting healthy cheap-sales firms against distressed cheap-sales firms. The low side is concentrated in firms where sales cheapness coincides with both liquidity pressure and cumulative loss history, rather than mixing in expensive firms with unrelated distress.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( mul( rank( ratio( revt, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), mul( indicator( sub( act, lct ), 0 ), indicator( re, 0 ) ) ), mul( rank( ratio( revt, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), mul( indicator( sub( lct, act ), 0 ), indicator( neg( re ), 0 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Relative-Pressure Sales Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(revt, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(TS_RANK(NEG(RATIO(lct, act)), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Revenue-cheap firms should perform better when current-liability pressure is low relative to the firm’s own recent history.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the working-capital-accrual change with a relative distress-state measure, avoiding the tension between working-capital release and liquidity cushion interpretations. Cheap sales are more likely to represent recoverable franchise value when the firm is not currently near a high-pressure point in its own short-term solvency cycle.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( revt, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ts_rank( neg( ratio( lct, act ) ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Stable Pretax-Capacity EBITDA Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(pi, lct), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: EBITDA-cheap firms should outperform when pretax income capacity relative to current liabilities is stable rather than volatile.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the liability-change derivative and tests a second-moment distress mechanism: instability of income available to meet near-term claims. Cheap EBITDA is more credible when pretax capacity is not swinging sharply relative to current liabilities, reducing the risk that the observed valuation is based on a temporary operating peak before distress.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( neg( vol( ratio( pi, lct ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Quality OCF Yield
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(che, act)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating-cash-flow yield should be most attractive when current assets are liquid cash rather than less reliable working-capital assets.
input_signals.reasoning: Prior OCF-liquidity evidence was strong, but current-asset composition may matter beyond total liquidity. A high cash share of current assets reduces the risk that apparent solvency depends on inventories or receivables that may not be realizable under distress.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( che, act ) ) )

input_signals.name: Retained-Capital Rebuild EBITDA Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(re, lt), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: EBITDA-cheap firms should outperform when retained capital is rebuilding relative to liabilities, indicating that distress is being repaired internally.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from a binary or continuous re-test of the static cash-minus-debt liquidity screen. The distress leg captures whether cumulative retained earnings are improving versus creditor claims, so cheap EBITDA is favored only when the residual equity claim is being rebuilt rather than hollowed out.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( delta( ratio( re, lt ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Rollover-Relief Sales Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(revt, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(dlc, lt), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Revenue-cheap firms should perform better when the fraction of liabilities due as short-term debt is falling.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the cash-quality/current-asset composition channel with a refinancing-risk channel that is independent of working-capital bloat. Cheap sales are more likely to represent recoverable franchise value when near-term debt pressure is receding rather than forcing equity dilution or distressed refinancing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( revt, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( neg( delta( ratio( dlc, lt ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cheap-Sales Balance-Sheet Trap
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(revt, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), SUMRANK(RATIO(lct, act), RATIO(NEG(re), lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: High revenue-to-price firms should underperform when sales cheapness coincides with both current-liability pressure and accumulated retained deficits.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the prior cash-flow polarity collapse by using two non-complementary distress dimensions: short-term solvency pressure and cumulative loss impairment. High values identify cheap-sales firms whose low valuation is more likely a distress signal than a compensated sales-yield opportunity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( revt, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), sumrank( ratio( lct, act ), ratio( neg( re ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Quality EBITDA Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(che, act)))
input_signals.hypothesis: EBITDA-cheap firms should outperform when their current assets are concentrated in cash rather than less reliable working-capital assets.
input_signals.reasoning: EBITDA yield has been the most successful valuation anchor, while cash-heavy current assets showed strong evidence when paired with OCF yield. This signal tests whether the cash-quality mechanism generalizes to operating earnings cheapness without relying on the prior cash-minus-debt-over-current-liabilities liquidity screen.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( che, act ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liability-Scale EBITDA Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(sale, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: EBITDA-cheap firms should outperform when their operating sales base is large relative to total liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from another temporal version of the cash-minus-short-debt liquidity screen. The distress leg asks whether creditor claims are supported by ongoing business scale, so high EBITDA yield is less likely to represent a thin equity stub behind excessive liabilities.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( sale, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Loss-Runway OCF Yield
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(lct, MAX(NEG(pi), 0)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating-cash-flow cheapness should be more reliable when cash can cover both near-term liabilities and any current pretax loss drain.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not an interpolation between cash-quality and cash-minus-debt conditioners; it measures survival runway against explicit current claims plus operating losses. Cheap operating cash flow is more likely to accrue to shareholders when the firm has enough cash to avoid forced financing while distress is being resolved.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( che, add( lct, max( neg( pi ), 0 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Percentile Weakest-Link OCF Safety
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MIN(RANK(RATIO(che, lct)), RANK(RATIO(ceq, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating-cash-flow yield should be rewarded only when both immediate liquidity and broader solvency are reasonably strong.
input_signals.reasoning: Ranking each safety dimension before applying MIN fixes the scale problem and makes the conditioner a true weakest-link comparison. Cheap cash-flow firms are penalized if either cash coverage of current liabilities or equity coverage of total liabilities is weak, because either constraint can turn value into distress.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), min( rank( ratio( che, lct ) ), rank( ratio( ceq, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Quality Distress-Price Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(lt, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(che, act)))
input_signals.hypothesis: High liabilities-to-market can be a compensated distress-value opportunity when the firm’s current assets are liquid.
input_signals.reasoning: Liabilities-to-market alone can describe either a levered value premium or a near-default equity stub. Conditioning it on cash-heavy current assets tests whether distress-priced firms are more likely to survive and let the leverage payoff accrue to equity holders.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( lt, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( che, act ) ) )

input_signals.name: Current-Deficit Adjusted EBITDA Yield
input_signals.expression: RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), MAX(SUB(lct, act), 0)))
input_signals.hypothesis: EBITDA cheapness should be rewarded when it remains high after penalizing firms with a current-liability deficit over current assets.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the loss-runway numerator swap with a claim-adjusted operating yield that focuses on negative working-capital gaps, not cash composition or pretax-loss coverage. Firms with high EBITDA relative to market equity plus any near-term funding deficit are less likely to be cheap only because current creditors have a near-term claim on the equity residual.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( ebitda, add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), max( sub( lct, act ), 0 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Tax-Validated Distress-Price Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(lt, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(txt, ADD(lct, MAX(NEG(pi), 0)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: High liabilities-to-market should be rewarded when the firm is still remitting taxes despite current-liability pressure and possible loss drains.
input_signals.reasoning: Liabilities-to-market can represent either compensated distress exposure or a near-default equity stub. Conditioning on tax payments relative to near-term claims and losses tests whether the highly levered cheap firm remains a taxable going concern rather than merely a distressed lottery ticket.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( lt, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( txt, add( lct, max( neg( pi ), 0 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Retained-Deficit Runway EBITDA Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(lct, MAX(NEG(re), 0)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: EBITDA-cheap firms should outperform when cash can cover current liabilities and any cumulative retained-deficit overhang.
input_signals.reasoning: The distress leg measures survival runway against both near-term claims and accumulated loss history, rather than only current cash composition. Cheap EBITDA is more likely to be recoverable value when the firm has enough cash to avoid being forced into financing because of creditor pressure or a deficit-ridden balance sheet.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( che, add( lct, max( neg( re ), 0 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Covered Sales Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(revt, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(che, lct)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Revenue-cheap firms should perform better when cash on hand is large relative to current liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: Sales-to-price has shown cross-sectional promise but can fail in portfolios when cheap sales belong to firms facing immediate liquidity stress. Conditioning on cash coverage of current liabilities focuses on revenue franchises that have enough liquidity runway for sales value to accrue to equity holders.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( revt, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( che, lct ) ) )

input_signals.name: Current-Claim Turnover EBITDA Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(revt, lct)))
input_signals.hypothesis: EBITDA-cheap firms should outperform when current liabilities are small relative to the firm’s revenue-generating scale.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids subtracting a balance-sheet stock from an operating flow and does not repackage the prior current-deficit adjusted yield. The distress leg measures current-claim turnover: cheap EBITDA is more likely to be a value opportunity when the operating franchise is large enough to absorb near-term obligations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( revt, lct ) ) )

input_signals.name: Loss-Runway Sales Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(revt, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(lct, MAX(NEG(pi), 0)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Revenue-cheap firms should outperform when cash can cover both near-term liabilities and any current pretax loss drain.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the dividend-yield anchor and its zero-payer rank mass entirely. The signal tests whether cheap sales are attached to firms with enough liquidity runway to survive current claims and operating losses, rather than firms whose low price-to-sales reflects imminent distress.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( revt, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( che, add( lct, max( neg( pi ), 0 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Margin-Secured Cash Sales Value
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(revt, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, revt)), RANK(RATIO(che, lct))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Revenue-cheap firms should outperform when sales are supported by positive operating margin and cash coverage of current liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: Sales-to-price has shown strong cross-sectional evidence but weak portfolio alpha, suggesting that cheap sales alone may include low-margin distressed firms.
